subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Should OpenClaw decouple Telegram runner sink concurrency from agents.defaults.maxConcurrent for multi-agent Telegram deployments, or keep the shared concurrency model and document supported tuning?
rationale: The source-backed remaining gap changes how channel ingress competes with agent execution, which is a product and operator-behavior choice rather than a mechanically safe bug fix without live proof.

options.title: Require live concurrency proof first
options.body: Capture a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before changing concurrency defaults or adding a new setting.

options.title: Decouple Telegram ingress
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned concurrency setting or derived default with live Telegram proof and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep shared concurrency
options.body: Leave the current maxConcurrent coupling in place and update diagnostics or docs around provider timeout and process-level tuning.

recommendation.title: Require live concurrency proof first
recommendation.body: Capture a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before changing concurrency defaults or adding a new setting.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining product decision is on the Telegram runner concurrency line currently attributed to Vincent Koc in local blame, though fallback-path owners should stay involved.
